Repent

rih-PENT -- shares a root with 'penitent,' meaning showing sorrow for wrongdoing. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To repent is to feel sincere regret for a wrongdoing and resolve to do better.

Faced with the damage he had caused, the young man finally began to repent for his reckless actions.

Worked Example

A person who spent years estranged from his family finally writes a long, honest letter apologizing for every hurtful thing he said, promising to be a better brother going forward.

That sincere regret paired with a genuine resolve to change is exactly what it means to repent. Unlike 'apologize,' which can be a quick, simple gesture, repent implies a deeper, more lasting change of heart.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

regret: to feel sorry about a past action

atone: to make amends for wrongdoing

reform: to make changes in order to improve

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

persist: to continue firmly in a course of action despite difficulty

relapse: to fall back into bad habits after improving

Where it sits · how far feeling turns into action — regret → repent → atone

regret vs. repent: Regret is milder than repent -- regret can be a private, passing feeling of sorrow, while repent implies a deeper, often public resolve to change one's behavior for good.

atone vs. repent: Atone can feel stronger than repent: repent focuses on the sincere feeling of regret and the resolve to change, while atone emphasizes actually making up for the wrongdoing through action.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: again; here an intensifier, 'thoroughly' (Latin)

Root — pent

Root — pent: penalty, punishment, sorrow (from Latin poena, 'penalty,' via paenitere, 'to cause regret')

Put it together

Put it together: Re- ('again' — here an intensifier, 'thoroughly') + pent ('penalty, sorrow' — from Latin poena via paenitere, 'to cause regret'): to repent, at its root, is to feel the weight of that penalty deeply enough to change — the same root that gives us penalty.

Use the root in a new word: penalty
